lesson.title: Escucha y Aplaude: A Listening and Clapping Game
lesson.subject: spanish

contentBlocks.text: Sol has ears ready to listen today — and so should you! We're going to play a clapping game with numbers.
When we say numbers out loud one at a time, we [[contar]] — that means 'to count'! Sol will say a number, and you'll clap that many times.
Listen for Sol's number: if Sol says tres, clap three times — ¡clap, clap, clap! Try it with uno, dos, tres, cuatro, and cinco.
You listened carefully and clapped the right number of times every time Sol said a number — that's what it means to contar! Tomorrow, we'll count real objects around the room.

config.instructions: Match the Spanish number to how many it means.

objectives: Clap the correct number of times (1-5) after hearing a spoken number
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Explain simply that contar means 'to count' — when we say numbers one after another, we're counting.
2. Have Sol say a number, e.g. '¡Tres!', and clap three times together with your child, counting the claps out loud: uno, dos, tres.
3. Take turns: Sol calls a number 1-5, your child claps that many times; then your child calls a number for Sol (or you) to clap.
4. Repeat with all five numbers in mixed-up order, moving faster once your child is confident.
5. Complete the on-screen matching activity together, reading each number aloud since your child may not read yet.
6. Close by asking: 'What does it mean to contar? Can you clap tres times for me?'
differentiationTips: Struggling: stick to uno, dos, tres for a few rounds before adding cuatro and cinco
Ready for more: call out two numbers in a row and have your child clap both counts back to back, e.g. dos, then cinco
Getting the clap count exactly right matters less than confidently attempting it — celebrate a close clap count as a win
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is a spoken-and-clapped listening activity — success looks like your child clapping close to the right number of times after hearing a number, not a written answer. In the matching game: uno → 1️⃣, dos → 2️⃣, tres → 3️⃣, cuatro → 4️⃣, cinco → 5️⃣, contar → 🔢 to count.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Continues week 3's WA-WL-2015.1.2 target by turning yesterday's counted fingers into pure listening comprehension — no visual number cue, just the spoken word — which is the heart of ACTFL Interpretive Listening, and introduces contar as the verb that names the whole week's activity.
